item.title: Starbucks pilots AI‑driven personalized drive‑thru menus
item.description:
Starbucks pilots AI‑driven personalized drive‑thru menus

Starbucks announced that it will experiment with artificial‑intelligence tools to recognize customers as they arrive at its drive‑thrus and serve each car a personalized digital menu.

🔍 Overview

  • The company plans to “recognize participating customers as they arrive, present personalized digital menus, and make payment more effortless” (CEO Brian Niccol, earnings call).
  • The effort is described as an early‑stage experiment that will be tested, learned from, and scaled if successful.

🛠️ How it works

  • Customer recognition – AI will identify a car or its occupants when they pull up to the lane.
  • Personalized menu display – A digital board will show menu items tailored to the recognized customer.
  • Background order‑entry AI (2027) – Starting in 2027, AI models will assist baristas in entering orders more accurately and efficiently.
  • App integration – AI will be added to the Starbucks app’s search and discovery features, with future support for “conversational and agentic” ordering.
  • Existing AI tools – Customers can already place orders through ChatGPT, and employees use the AI‑powered Green Dot Assist for recipe and service‑standard queries.

📋 Features

  • Recognize customers at the drive‑thru entrance.
  • Show a personalized digital menu per car.
  • Streamline payment and order entry.
  • Test background AI models for barista assistance beginning in 2027.
  • Expand AI to app search, discovery, and conversational ordering.
  • Existing ChatGPT ordering channel and employee‑focused Green Dot Assist.

📊 Comparison with peers

Company AI Drive‑Thru Feature Personalization Detail
Starbucks Recognize customers, display personalized digital menu, background order‑entry AI (2027) Car‑by‑car menu customization based on identified customer
Taco Bell Experiments with menu boards that change layout, content, visuals on a car‑by‑car basis Similar car‑specific visual changes
McDonald’s “ArchIQ” chatbot identifies repeat customers and lets them order their “usual” Repeat‑customer ordering via chatbot

🚀 Timeline / Availability

  • Now – Announcement and early testing phase (CEO calls it “early”).
  • 2027 – Planned testing of background AI models for order entry.
  • Future – Potential rollout of personalized digital menus after testing; exact launch date not disclosed.

💡 Why it matters

  • Enhances individual customer experience at high‑traffic drive‑thrus.
  • Aims to reduce order errors and speed up service.
  • Extends AI use beyond internal tools to visible consumer‑facing interfaces.
  • Signals broader industry interest in AI‑driven personalization (as seen at Taco Bell and McDonald’s).

#Starbucks #AI #DriveThru #Personalization

Source: Starbucks wants to use AI to show you a ‘personalized digital menu’ at the drive-thru

item.title: Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout
item.description:
Shopify Expands Catalog Access to AI Agents for Automated Shopping and Checkout

Shopify announced Tuesday it will allow shoppers to configure AI agents to purchase products on their behalf, giving these agents access to a catalog of over a billion listings. This development marks an expansion of the company’s agentic commerce ambitions, moving beyond a previous exclusive partnership with Meta’s Muse agent. Users can now utilize any AI agent for browsing and purchasing without a specific partnership integration.

🔍 Overview

Shopify is marketing the new feature as a “personal shopper” that can act on a human’s behalf. The agent has access to a catalog consisting of items located both on and off Shopify storefronts. This move follows an earlier partnership announced in September with Meta to allow the Muse agent to browse and purchase items.

🧩 How it works

To enable automated shopping, customers must connect an AI agent to their account on Shop, a Shopify-owned platform designed to consolidate orders and track packages.

  • Integration: The agent connects directly to the user’s Shop account.
  • Checkout: Transactions occur via the one-click Shop Pay feature within the conversation with the agent.
  • Order Management: Any orders placed by the agent are funneled back to the Shop app for tracking.

⚙️ Key details

Humans remain in control of the agent’s behavior through specific rules and required authorizations:

  • Budget Guardrails: Users can set spending limits for the agent.
  • Shipping Preferences: Users can instruct agents to only display products with fast shipping.
  • Purchase Approval: Buyers are required to approve each purchase before it is finalized.

💡 Why it matters

E-commerce has emerged as a significant battleground for AI development, with companies like Google and Amazon also investing in tools where the end goal is an autonomous agent purchasing items for users. This shift has also sparked conflict between major commerce players and AI companies, such as the ongoing dispute between Amazon and firms like Perplexity and Meta over whether agents should be permitted to shop on a customer’s behalf.

#Shopify #AIagents #ECommerce #ShopPay #AgenticCommerce

Source: Shopify opens its catalog up to more AI agents

item.title: Square launches Square Kiosk with conversational AI ordering interface
item.description:
Square launches Square Kiosk with conversational AI ordering interface

Square announced a new hardware product that blends a large touchscreen kiosk with a conversational AI assistant for ordering.

🔍 Overview

  • The device is called the Square Kiosk.
  • It is a big kiosk with a 21.5‑inch touchscreen and a pill‑shaped form factor.
  • An “agentic, conversational voice layer” lets customers talk to the AI as they would to staff.

🧩 How it works

  • Presence detection greets customers as they approach the kiosk.
  • While speaking with the AI agent, users can:
    • Ask questions about the menu.
    • Request modifications and substitutions.
    • Receive real‑time responses that fully understand the seller’s menu.
  • When ordering is complete, payment can be made via a contactless payment reader or a card slot.

⚙️ Key details

  • Screen size: 21.5 inches.
  • Form factor: Large pill shape.
  • AI capabilities: Real‑time listening, menu comprehension, natural‑language ordering.
  • Payment options: Contactless reader and card slot.

🚀 Availability

  • The Square Kiosk is available starting today.
  • Price: $1,999 per device for businesses with a Square Plus or Premium subscription.
  • Ongoing software fee: $99 per device per month.

#Square #AI #Kiosk #Payments #ConversationalAI

Source: Square’s new kiosk lets you talk to AI for help with your order

item.title: Walmart Denies Use of Personalized Pricing with Digital Shelf Labels
item.description:
Walmart Denies Use of Personalized Pricing with Digital Shelf Labels

Walmart has stated it will not use personal information or time of day to change product prices, following reports from The Wall Street Journal.

⚙️ Key details

In a letter to customers, CEO John Furner clarified the purpose and limitations of the company’s pricing strategies:

  • Digital Shelf Labels: The rollout of these labels in all US stores by the end of the year is intended to save store associates time, not to dynamically change prices.
  • Pricing Constraints: Prices will not be changed based on:
    • Personal income
    • Shopping history
    • Urgency
    • Perceived ability to pay
    • Time of day (e.g., a hot afternoon)
    • Sudden rushes for an item
  • AI Integration: Walmart will not use conversations with its Sparky AI assistant to change prices.

💡 Why it matters

The company’s reassurance comes amid increasing regulatory scrutiny:

  • Federal Level: The Federal Trade Commission is developing a policy to clamp down on personalized pricing.
  • State Level:
    • New York requires retailers to disclose the use of algorithmic pricing.
    • New Jersey, Connecticut, and Maryland have moved to ban the use of personal data to change store prices.

#Walmart #AI #PersonalizedPricing #RetailTech

Source: Walmart won’t hike prices based on your shopping history, CEO says

item.title: Automating Retail Replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick
item.description:
Automating Retail Replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick

A new technical solution integrates Databricks and Amazon Quick to automate the retail replenishment loop, connecting demand forecasting directly to order placement to reduce stockouts of fast-moving items.

💡 Why it matters

Retail demand forecasts typically have a short shelf life. Traditionally, the gap between a forecast and a placed order persisted because the forecast (stored in a governed data platform) and supplier availability (stored in a separate operational feed) lived in different systems, often inaccessible to the person placing the order. While foundation models have simplified demand forecasting across entire catalogs without per-item tuning, the bottleneck shifted to the downstream gap between the forecast and the action.

🧩 How it works

The solution creates a loop that detects demand surges, identifies a supplier, and places orders unattended, escalating to a human only when no rule fits. The process runs in four stages:

Stage Tool Function
Forecast Databricks MMF Serves Chronos-2 to predict 7-day demand for every SKU.
Detect Databricks Genie Agent Surfaces SKUs in a surge (next-7-day average $\geq$ 1.5x prior-14-day average, with a floor of 1).
Decide Amazon Quick Reconciles surging SKUs against live supplier availability in Amazon S3 Tables and picks the cheapest supplier.
Act Amazon Quick Flows Places a purchase order via Supplier Order API or raises a human-review ticket if no single supplier can cover the surge.

Amazon Quick serves as the central component, joining data on a shared product key at decision time using a Databricks Genie Agent over the Model Context Protocol (MCP), S3 Tables for supplier feeds, and an OpenAPI connector for the Order API.

⚙️ Key details

Technical Requirements:

  • Databricks CLI 0.299.0+
  • AWS CLI 2.36.2+
  • jq 1.7
  • uv (or Python 3.11) for the supplier-feed loader

Permissions and Setup:

  • Amazon Quick: User requires an Author or Author Pro role to create Quick Flows, MCP, and OpenAPI connectors.
  • Databricks: Identity requires CREATE CATALOG on the metastore (or admin pre-creation of the mmf catalog).
  • Authentication: Databricks workspace profile must be authenticated via databricks auth login.

Deployment: The solution is managed via the local terminal using aws quicksight subcommands (create-flow, create-data-source, and create-space). Key files in the accompanying repository include genie/genie_space for the agent definition, flow/flow_definition for the flow, and cleanup/cleanup.sh for teardown. The forecast is produced using notebooks 01 and 02 from the MMF accelerator’s fresh_retail_net example.

#Databricks #AmazonQuick #RetailAutomation #SupplyChain #DemandForecasting

Source: Automate replenishment with MMF, Databricks Genie, and Amazon Quick | Amazon Web Services
